cur:catacombs-arles-farewell.summary: A crowded relief shows Christ at the centre among the apostles who press around him, with smaller figures kneeling below. The museum identifies the subject as Christ's farewell to his apostles.
facts: The museum describes the piece as an 'element of a sarcophagus representing Christ's farewell to his apostles'.
A separate small fragment is mounted at its upper left.
cur:catacombs-arles-farewell.notes: The identification of the subject follows the museum's title.

cur:manuscripts-egberti-canaanite-woman.summary: A woman, labelled 'Chananaea', approaches with hands raised in supplication, while Christ, flanked by Peter and other apostles, turns toward her. The empty ground between them heightens the drama of her plea.
facts: The Codex Egberti, a Gospel lectionary made for Archbishop Egbert of Trier, is described as the oldest surviving New Testament picture cycle of the life of Christ in the Ottonian era: 52 of its 60 paintings illustrate Gospel readings in the order of the church year.
Seven of its miniatures are attributed to the anonymous 'Master of the Registrum Gregorii', who worked in Trier.
